# Sirach Chapter 23 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 23 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**Council Notes:**
Chapter 23 consists of three movements: a prayer for discipline over speech and desire (vv. 1-6), instruction on oaths and coarse language (vv. 7-15), and a section on sexual infidelity — male (vv. 16-21) and female (vv. 22-28). The prayer in vv. 1-6 is among the most personal in Sirach. The "eyes of the LORD are ten thousand times brighter than the sun" (v. 18) is one of the great theological affirmations of divine omniscience. Note: v. 28 is bracketed in some MSS as a secondary addition.

---

**23:1** O LORD, Father and Master of my life, do not abandon me to their counsel; do not let me fall because of them.

**23:2** Who will set stripes over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over my heart, to spare me nothing in my acts of ignorance and not to overlook my sins?

**23:3** Lest my acts of ignorance multiply and my sins abound, and I fall before my enemies while my adversary rejoices over me.

**23:4** O LORD, Father and God of my life, do not give me arrogant eyes; turn desire away from me.

**23:5** Let not desire for food and for sexual union take hold of me; do not hand me over to a shameless spirit.

**23:6** Give ear, children, to the discipline of the mouth; whoever keeps it will not be ensnared.

**23:7** In his sins the sinner is trapped; the proud man and the blasphemer stumble in them.

**23:8** Do not accustom your mouth to swearing oaths, and do not make it a habit to name the Holy One.

**23:9** For as a slave who is continually questioned will not lack for bruises, so one who always swears and invokes the Name will never be free from sin.

**23:10** A man who swears much will be filled with iniquity, and the scourge will not depart from his house. If he offends, his sin is upon him; if he ignores it, he has sinned doubly; and if he swore in vain, he will not be acquitted, for his house will be filled with calamities.

**23:11** There is a manner of speech clothed about with death; may it not be found in the inheritance of Jacob. For all these things will be far from the godly, and they will not wallow in sins.

**23:12** Do not accustom your mouth to crude language, for in it there is sinful speech.

**23:13** Remember your father and your mother, for you sit in the midst of great people; and lest you forget yourself before them and through force of habit behave foolishly, and wish you had never been born, and curse the day of your birth.

**23:14** A man who is accustomed to abusive language will not be disciplined all his days.

**23:15** Two kinds of people multiply sins, and a third brings on wrath: a soul burning like fire will not be quenched until it consumes; a man of fornication in the body of his flesh will not cease until the fire burns out.

**23:16** All bread is sweet to the fornicator; he will not tire of it until he dies.

**23:17** A man who strays from his own bed says in his heart, "Who sees me? Darkness surrounds me, the walls cover me, and no one sees me. What do I have to fear? The Most High will not remember my sins."

**23:18** His eyes are on human eyes, but he does not consider that the eyes of the LORD are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, observing all the ways of men and searching into hidden places.

**23:19** All things were known before they were created, and likewise after they were completed.

**23:20** This man will be punished in the streets of the city, and seized where he least expected it.

**23:21** So too the woman who abandoned her husband and provided an heir by a stranger.

**23:22** For first she was disobedient to the law of the Most High; second, she sinned against her husband; and third, she committed adultery in fornication and provided children by another man.

**23:23** She herself will be brought before the assembly, and a reckoning will come upon her children.

**23:24** Her children will not take root, and her branches will bear no fruit.

**23:25** She will leave behind her memory as a curse, and her disgrace will never be blotted out.

**23:26** And those who remain will know: there is nothing better than the fear of the LORD, and nothing sweeter than to keep the commandments of the LORD.

**23:27** It is a great glory to follow after the LORD; and length of days is received from him.

**23:28** Whoever does these things will inherit praise, for the fear of the LORD leads to life and lets one rest through the night undisturbed.
